newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE BATTLING TO AVOID INNINGS DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE BATTLING TO AVOID INNINGS DEFEAT.

text.p: Zimbabwe, needing 178 to avoid an innings defeat, battled to 124 for three at lunch on the fifth and final day of the first test against Pakistan on Monday.
Fast bowler Waqar Younis broke through with the ninth delivery of the morning after the touring team resumed their second innings at 38 for one.
He captured his first wicket of the match by trapping Alistair Campbell lbw for 15 after the Zimbabwe captain had added just a single to his overnight score.
However, Grant Flower, who made 110 in the first innings, and David Houghton defied Pakistan in a third wicket stand of 84 before off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq ended their resistance.
Flower, playing a defensive shot, was caught by Shadab Kabir at short leg immediately before lunch. His 46 contained eight fours and occupied 147 balls.
At the break Houghton was on 44 and Andy Flower had yet to open his account.
